claim.purpose: Repair the Opus review runbook and add a focused interface drift check

initial.title: [v0.91.8][provider][docs] Keep Opus review runbook aligned with adapter CLI
initial.goal: Make the Opus review procedure match the current Rust provider adapter interface and remain resistant to CLI drift.
initial.required_outcome: A source-grounded runbook and focused contract check document and verify the structured JSON adapter invocation.
authority_boundary: Issue 5678 owns only the runbook and its focused contract check
Provider implementation and lifecycle authority remain unchanged
initial.task_boundary: Repair the bounded runbook and verify its CLI/schema claims.
acceptance_criteria: AC-2: JSON example names Anthropic Opus, model identity, bounded attempts, and exact-head review input
AC-3: Credential handling is one-command and secret-free
AC-4: Focused contract check detects stale flags or missing request fields
AC-5: Docs-only validation and exact review pass before publication
dependencies: Current adl-provider-adapter CLI source and provider communication request schema
non_goals: No live credential or network probe
initial.plan_summary: Read the actual CLI and request schema, write a concise tracked runbook, add a focused contract check, validate docs hygiene, obtain exact review, and publish.

steps.action: Bind issue 5678 with disjoint documentation and test paths
Repair the tracked Opus runbook from current Rust source evidence
Add and run the focused CLI/schema contract check
Run exact review and publish only after findings are resolved

invariants: No secrets or absolute local paths are recorded
Provider success is never inferred from adapter invocation alone
risks: CLI or request schema drift can stale the procedure
A prompt summary can be mistaken for source evidence
The ignored operator-local TBD mirror can diverge from the tracked canonical runbook
stop_conditions: A requested change needs provider credentials or AWS
Work would touch provider implementation or lifecycle code

validation_lanes.proof_role: Verify documented adapter flags, JSON fields, credential handling, and review truth boundaries against source text
Verify the bounded documentation diff has no whitespace corruption

initial.failure_policy: Fail closed on stale interface claims, missing schema evidence, secret or absolute-path leakage, scope drift, or failed focused validation.
review_prompts: Does the runbook invoke the actual JSON CLI?
Can an operator verify provider/model identity and exact revision without exposing secrets?
Does the contract check fail when the CLI interface drifts?
